en.title: Xbox Accessibility Team Faces Uncertainty After Major Layoffs Raise Concerns
en.summary: Recent layoffs at Xbox have jeopardized its award‑winning accessibility initiatives, sparking concern among disability advocates. In parallel, New Mexico officials are urged to adopt universal design and staff training to improve government accessibility, while the Library of Congress recognized accessible libraries in Georgia and Massachusetts. Additionally, ITRI’s inclusive cycling event and a report linking accessibility bugs to architectural flaws highlight ongoing progress and challenges.

highlights.title: Layoffs Leave Future of Xbox’s Award-Winning Accessibility Efforts in Doubt
Op-Ed: Making New Mexico Government More Accessible for Persons with Disabilities
Library of Congress Program Honors Accessible Libraries in Georgia and Massachusetts
ITRI's public welfare initiative brings together 115 participants with disabilities for a group cycling event, promoting inclusion and showcasing adaptive cycling as a dream-fulfilling activity
Accessibility Bugs Are Often Architecture Bugs

zh-TW.title: Xbox 無障礙團隊面臨裁員衝擊，未來存疑引發關注
zh-TW.summary: Xbox 近期裁員影響其獲獎無障礙計畫，引發外界對其未來發展的擔憂。同時，新墨西哥政府被呼籲採用普遍設計與員工培訓提升無障礙服務，而國會圖書館表彰喬治亞州與麻薩諸塞州的無障礙圖書館。此外，工研院的共融騎乘活動以及社群討論創傷知識照護的缺失，共同凸顯無障礙領域的進步與挑戰。
